chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Dinah Shore and Peggy Lee as listeners of her style
summary: Dinah Shore acknowledged her as a major influence; Peggy Lee also mentioned her; she was influenced by Ella, Billie and Ethel Waters.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: There's a whole bunch of other names I suppose I could throw at you but I think I got the general idea. How about one more, Dinah Shore.

Dinah Shore? I'm not too sure. Dinah came along at the same time that I did. I have a feeling that there was a group of singers that came along at the same time I did who were probably coached along the lines that I would be singing, you know. They probably were told to and maybe they listened to some of my recordings, because if you listen closely the quality is the same. I think the way they approached a song would be the same way I would approach a song.

People like Dinah Shore and some others who, you know, did three or four things and then you never heard from them again. But, well we know for certainty that after, Flow Gently, Sweet Rhythm Program that we had on the air, another program started, Street what, the Chamber Music of Lower Basin/ or something like that. And Dinah Shore was the singer. And the format was basically the same.
That's the way we feel about it, you know.
I was reading in the George

That's possible. I did come before Dinah Shore. I do detect in her renditions alot of the approaches I might have done. The only thing about it, I don't think she's as musically inclined as I would be.
I just wanted to put on the tape at least that's one person I came up with who acknowledged that you were a major influence. Are there any others that you know of?

Yeah, Peggy Lee at one time mentioned that fact. But Peggy Lee, see when I was in the Le Ruban Bleu, Dave Barber with whom she married was the guitar player. Of course Peggy would be in the club quite often. Peggy was singing at the time but she may have listened. There's nothing unusual about singers being influenced by other singers.
I mean, you are. I'm influenced. I was influenced by Ella, Billie, Ethel Waters. I liked to take a little bit of everybody's style and
